[04:35] Daniel Kim: can you repeat the per-token? i'm used to seeing dollars, not micro-dollars, that's confusing.

[06:10] Maria Lopez: what about latency tradeoffs if we batch more? some of our internal tools need sub-150ms p50 which seems tough.
[06:18] Priya Rao: right, batching increases throughput but adds queuing. for low-latency routes we recommend smaller batch sizes, dynamic batching with a 20-50ms trigger. Redwood runtime supports continuous batching and can be tuned. for the POC we can set two routes: low-latency (p50 goal 120-150ms) and high-throughput for analytics where batching to 4-8 inferences helps cost.

[08:02] Kevin Hart: and caching? we have a lot of repeated prefixes for system prompts. can prefix cache shave off cost?
[08:09] Priya Rao: yes, prefix/KV cache is huge. if your workload has repeated context, we can cache the KV for the prefix and only compute the new tokens. depending on reuse, you can save 30-70% of tokens billed on average. small note: sometimes the transcript system spells KV as "KV cash" or similar, so docs have a typo, sorry.

[10:20] Alex Chen: on deployment modes: hosted API for fast POC is easiest and gives us performance baselines. Dedicated reserved capacity drops unit cost and gives predictability; Private (VPC) is possible for later stages if you need on-prem or strict residency. any red flags on compliance?
[10:46] Kevin Hart: we need SOC2 + audit logs, SSO via SAML, and KMS integration. also network peering for Private or dedicated.
[10:55] Alex Chen: good — Redwood supports SAML, full audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations, and Private with customer-managed networking. we'll share the security pack.

[13:40] Priya Rao: quick calc: 200k tokens/day * per-token cost. if hosted at $0.001 per token average, that's $200/day ~$6k/month. But if we tune batching and move to Dedicated we might cut unit cost in half, so ~$3k/month, plus reserved infra fees. But that rough math ignores caching; with a 40% cache hit you drop billable tokens to 120k, so $120/day -> big savings.

[22:38] Priya Rao: main things: network peering IP ranges, KMS connectivity, and if on-prem you'll need to allow RPMs for our runtime. Also watch out for NTP/time sync — weird but matters for tracing. We'll share a checklist.

[27:48] Priya Rao: for closed models, those providers can be cheaper per token in some cases, but you lose routing flexibility and dedicated capacity control. Also with open models and quantization on Dedicated we often see better price-performance for heavy workloads. we'll include a simple TCO comparison in the spreadsheet.

[42:06] Priya Rao: cache itself doesn't get you billed for elided tokens. Billing is on emitted compute tokens; the cache reduces compute. There are small metadata costs for cache storage in Dedicated but negligible relative to compute.
